**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate available-first selection on the linked credit-card type**

When a user turns this option on for a card, unlinks it, and then relinks the surviving `EnableBankingAccount` to a manual non-credit account such as a Depository, the provider row retains the true flag. This line therefore selects CLAV/ITAV for that non-card even though `EnableBankingAccount::Processor#process_account!` only interprets the flag inside its `CreditCard` branch; the depository records the overdraft-inclusive available amount directly, regressing the booked-first safeguard and shifting net worth/history. Include the linked account type in this predicate so every non-card remains booked-first.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Reviewed the diff and the surrounding `EnableBankingAccount`/`EnableBankingAccount::Processor` code. The core fix is correct: `AVAILABLE_CREDIT_BALANCE_TYPE_PRIORITY = (%w[CLAV ... ITAV ... XPCD ...] + BALANCE_TYPE_PRIORITY).uniq.freeze` correctly dedupes so CLAV/ITAV/XPCD are tried first and the booked types still serve as fallback, and the new tests exercise both the mBank scenario and the booked-only fallback.

A couple of notes beyond Codex's existing finding:

- Codex's P1 comment on `importer.rb:248` (gating `prefer_available` on the flag alone, not on the linked account's type) checks out — I confirmed `treat_balance_as_available_credit` is a plain boolean column on `enable_banking_accounts` with no model-level validation or callback tying it to a `CreditCard`-typed linked account (`app/models/enable_banking_account.rb`), unlike `EnableBankingAccount::Processor#interpret_credit_card_balance`, which only applies the flag's special handling inside the `accountable_type == "CreditCard"` branch. So a relink to a Depository/Investment account (or any out-of-band flag flip) would make the importer prefer an available-type balance for a non-card account, which is exactly the overdraft-inflation case the existing `BALANCE_TYPE_PRIORITY` comment warns about. Worth gating on `account.accountable_type == "CreditCard"` the same way `process_account!` does, or clearing the flag on unlink.
- Separately: `AVAILABLE_CREDIT_BALANCE_TYPE_PRIORITY` puts `XPCD` ahead of the booked types (`CLBD`/`ITBD`/`OPBD`/`PRCD`), whereas in the default priority `XPCD` ranks below all booked types. The PR description/comments don't say whether an ASPSP's "expected" balance is known to represent available credit (vs. an expected booked debt) for available-credit-mode cards — if that's unconfirmed, it's a plausible source of a similar booked-vs-available mix-up to the one this PR fixes. No test currently exercises a response containing both `XPCD` and a booked type under `prefer_available: true`, so it's not obvious from the test suite whether this ordering was deliberate.

Nothing else to add on tenancy/security or conventions — no controller/API surface touched, and `DebugLogEntry` usage is unchanged.
